milestones.title: Agent registry and global-default resolution are durable and inspectable
milestones.goal: A human can create an always-on agent, get an auto-generated id when omitted, persist provider/model/thinking defaults, and reliably resolve one global default agent from append-only facts.

verification.command: Review the always-on agent registry/global-default implementation against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review finds the milestone correct or yields actionable blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: In a temp MU_CODING_AGENT_DIR and temp workspace, run `mu always-on create --workspace <path> --provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.4 --thinking medium`, then create a second agent and use `mu always-on set-default <agent-id>`; verify the generated ids, provider/model/thinking details, and global default designation appear correctly in terminal output.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface shows first-create auto-default behavior and later explicit global default changes correctly.

verification.command: Inspect agents.jsonl in a temp config dir and assert append-only facts resolve to exactly one global default agent at a time.
verification.expect: Derived global-default resolution matches the visible CLI output and raw ledger facts.

milestones.notes: The gate task closes this milestone only after ledger derivation, global-default behavior, CLI output, and review are all green.

milestones.title: Immediate work submission creates a durable run and linked Mu thread
milestones.goal: A human can send immediate work to an always-on agent, optionally override the provider/model/thinking tuple for that work item, and observe a durable work item, durable run lifecycle, and linked Mu session/thread.

verification.command: npm test -w @kennyfrc/mu-coding-agent -- always-on-send-run.red.test.ts always-on-supervisor.red.test.ts always-on-execution-target.red.test.ts always-on-tool-selection.red.test.ts
verification.expect: Immediate send/run lifecycle tests pass, including linked session id creation, terminal outcome recording, execution-tuple override precedence, and always-on tool selection that excludes ask_user.

verification.command: Review immediate send/run orchestration, execution-target override precedence, lock ownership, always-on tool selection, and Mu session linkage against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the send-to-run lifecycle, tuple-override precedence, and no-ask_user tool policy are correct or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: In a temp MU_CODING_AGENT_DIR and temp workspace, create a default agent using `--provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.4 --thinking low`, run `mu always-on send --provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.4 --thinking medium "<instruction>"`, then inspect `mu always-on jobs`, `mu always-on runs <job-id>`, and visible terminal output.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface shows created job/run ids, linked session/thread information, and that the run used the explicit invocation override (`openai-codex / gpt-5.4 / medium`) rather than the stored default thinking level.

verification.command: Inspect work-items.jsonl, runs.jsonl, and the linked Mu session file for the run; assert that work item override fields, run lifecycle, effective provider/model/thinking tuple, session id, and terminal outcome all agree.
verification.expect: Raw ledgers and Mu session history agree on the executed run and its effective execution tuple.

milestones.notes: The gate task closes this milestone only after immediate send-to-run behavior is proven through tests, raw-ledger assertions, and visible CLI output.

milestones.title: Scheduled work runs with latest-missed, single-overlap, and restart-replacement semantics
milestones.goal: One-off and recurring schedules produce due runs with latest-missed-only catch-up, exactly one queued overlap occurrence, and replacement-run recovery after crash while the supervisor uses event wake plus periodic reconciliation tick instead of model polling.

verification.expect: Schedule parsing, latest-missed derivation, single-overlap queuing, reconciliation tick, replacement-run recovery, and occurrence deduplication tests pass.

verification.command: Review scheduling, latest-missed policy, overlap policy, occurrence-key derivation, reconciliation tick behavior, and restart handling against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms no duplicate occurrence execution, correct backlog/overlap policy, and no incorrect model polling, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: In a temp MU_CODING_AGENT_DIR and temp workspace, schedule one one-off job and one recurring job, observe terminal output and status/jobs output before and after due time, and verify only the latest missed occurrence is run and the same occurrence is not shown twice after reconciliation.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface shows due work running at the expected times with latest-missed-only and no duplicate occurrence reporting.

verification.command: Simulate a crash after `run_started` and before `run_finished`, restart the supervisor, and assert from runs.jsonl that the interrupted run is marked abandoned/errored, a replacement run is created, and the occurrence key still appears exactly once for the successful occurrence.
verification.expect: Restart and reconciliation preserve accepted work, create a replacement run, and avoid duplicating the same scheduled occurrence.

milestones.notes: The gate task closes this milestone only after schedule/tick correctness is proven under fake-clock and restart conditions, not just ad-hoc manual timing.

milestones.title: Follow-ups, history inspection, and thread linkage remain correct and inspectable
milestones.goal: A human can follow up on a past job, inherit the prior effective execution tuple by default, inspect jobs/runs/thread lineage, and rely on linked Mu session/thread semantics plus completion/blocker notifications.

verification.expect: Follow-up lineage, tuple inheritance, jobs/runs inspection, linked thread references, and notification tests pass.

verification.command: Review follow-up creation, tuple inheritance, lineage projection, run/thread inspection, and notification behavior against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the milestone is functionally correct, including tuple inheritance defaults, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: In a temp MU_CODING_AGENT_DIR and temp workspace, create work with a non-default execution tuple, run a follow-up via `mu always-on follow-up <job-id> "..."` without restating the tuple, then inspect `jobs`, `runs <job-id>`, `status`, and the thread inspection surface.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface shows follow-up lineage, inherited effective tuple, linked prior job/run references, and thread/session ids clearly.

verification.command: Use the resulting run session ids with existing Mu thread inspection semantics and assert that the linked history remains readable and correctly associated with the originating jobs.
verification.expect: Jobs, runs, and Mu thread/session history remain linked and inspectable without special-case transcript formats.

milestones.notes: The gate task closes this milestone only after follow-up lineage, notifications, and thread inspection are all proven through tests and visible CLI evidence.
